title: Permission attenuation and forensics runbook
content:
Purpose
This doc captures a pragmatic operational runbook for permission attenuation (time/usage-scoped reductions of granted entitlements), the forensic evidence we must emit to support audits/SIEM, and a staged rollout approach for RBAC v2 components that touches user-facing entitlements and the audit pipeline.

Context and motivating problems
- We need a way to automatically reduce privileges for high-risk actions when certain signals occur (e.g., suspicious session, unusual API patterns, geolocation mismatch) without fully revoking access.
- Audit evidence today is noisy: too many flattened logs, inconsistent fields, and gaps during transient permission changes (canaries/cutovers).
- Security/Compliance teams require deterministic, queryable artifacts for attestation windows (30/90/365 day) and forensics.
- We must avoid increased latency on the request path while ensuring attenuation decisions are verifiable and auditable.

Design goals (priority order)
1) Minimal request latency impact (<= 3ms additional wall time for auth checks)
2) Deterministic, time-indexed evidence records that map to a single change/event id
3) Reproducible attenuation logic (policy inputs, signals, decision rationale) stored alongside evidence
4) Smooth rollback path for mistaken attenuations and ability to retroactively annotate evidence
5) SIEM-friendly export format (consistent schema, parsable timestamps, stable field names)

High-level approach
- Introduce an attenuation layer in the authorization pipeline: a lightweight policy evaluation that outputs an attenuation token (AT) when relevant. The runtime uses AT to apply temporary constraints (reduced scopes, rate-limits, timebound allowlists).
- Emit three linked artifacts per attenuation event: 1) decision record (immutable), 2) active-enforcement marker (ephemeral TTL aligned with attenuation window), 3) audit snapshot (user+resource+policy version + request context). Each artifact must contain the same event_id GUID.
- SIEM export: batch and streaming modes supported. Batch (hourly) for historical indexing; streaming (Kafka-like) for real-time monitoring and SOAR triggers.

Permission model notes (how attenuation maps to RBAC v2 primitives)
- Roles remain coarse-grained; attenuation produces temporary attribute constraints that sit on the AccessRequest object. Example: role=platform-admin + attenuation{deny: [account.delete], allow: [read], until: 2024-03-12T15:04:05Z}
- Attenuation tokens are signed (HMAC + key id) and include: event_id, expires_at, policy_hash, reason_code, issued_by, version. This allows services to verify integrity without consulting the central policy store on every request.
- Policy determinism: policy_hash references a deterministic serialization of the policy logic (protobuf canonical form). This avoids ambiguity during audits.

SIEM / audit schema (key fields we will standardize)
- event_id: string (GUID)
- emitted_at: ISO8601 timestamp (UTC)
- actor_id: user/service principal id
- actor_role_snapshot: semicolon-delimited list (role@version)
- target_resource: resource path (e.g., projects/123/models/abcd)
- action_requested: verb (e.g., model.delete)
- attenuation_applied: boolean
- attenuation_details: semicolon-delimited key=value pairs (deny=[...];allow=[...];until=...;policy_hash=...)
- decision_rationale: short free text (max 512 chars)
- policy_version: canonical id
- enforcement_node: region/host id
- evidence_refs: semicolon-delimited list of related event_ids (e.g., prior signals)
- signature_kid: key id used to sign AT
- raw_request_context_url: (signed link to ephemeral request dump for SRE/forensics)

Note: fields use stable names; SIEM ingestion mapping will normalize timestamps and flatten attenuation_details into top-level fields where needed.

Evidence automation runbook (ops steps for incident or audit request)
1) Detection/Trigger: internal signal sets attenuation via policy engine (examples: anomalous-rate, credential-pairing-mismatch). Event_id generated.
2) Immediate emission: decision record + active-enforcement marker + audit snapshot emitted to emit-topic (streaming) and persisted to evidence-store (cold tier) with retention metadata.
3) Notify: send webhook to security-alerts channel and create Jira ticket (auto-template) when severity>=HIGH.
4) Forensics: SRE can request an evidence package (evidence-store returns zipped artifacts + signed chain-of-trust metadata). Use event_id as the index.
5) Attestation: for compliance requests, generate an attestation bundle that includes policy_hash, policy source link, and a human-readable rationale. Bundle is stored under evidence-retention/attestations/{year}/{event_id}.zip

Rollout strategy (staged and reversible)
- Phase 0 (lab): test harness and deterministic policy serialization. Unit and fuzz tests cover policy edge-cases. No production emissions.
- Phase 1 (shadow emission): policy engine emits attenuation tokens and audit artifacts, but enforcement is no-op (service reads AT but ignores). SIEM receives artifacts. Validate schema, cardinality, and downstream parsers. Duration: 2 weeks.
- Phase 2 (observed enforcement): select low-risk routes (read-only) apply attenuations as soft-deny (service returns warning headers and logs a metric). Monitor false positives. Duration: 3-4 weeks.
- Phase 3 (canary enforcement): 3% of write traffic across two regions. Automatic rollback trigger if SLOs (latency/pp95 error) deviate beyond threshold or if false positive rate > 0.5%.
- Phase 4 (global enforcement): full rollout with policy freeze window and post-rollout attestation generation.

Rollback and remediation patterns
- Fast rollback: central policy toggles to disable attenuation decisions generation (minutes). Services configured to drop AT acceptance when disabled to avoid stale tokens.
- Patch mitigation: if specific policy_hash causes high FP, use override whitelist that maps event_id -> remediation_action and annotate evidence with override_id.
- Forensic correction: evidence entries are immutable, but we will support annotation records that reference event_id and provide human review notes (annotator_id, timestamp, summary). These annotations are stored in a separate index and exported alongside attestation bundles.

Operational checks and metrics to instrument
- attenuation_events_emitted (counter) by reason_code
- attenuation_applied_success (counter, per service)
- attenuation_verification_latency_ms (histogram)
- false_positive_rate (derived from security reviewer labels)
- evidence_export_failures (counter)
- SIEM_ingest_lag_seconds (gauge)

Testing and validation plan
- Property-based tests for policy determinism (random policies -> canonical serialization -> policy_hash stability)
- End-to-end replay of historical traffic (staging) to validate artifact completeness
- SIEM downstream contract tests (mock SIEM parses sample messages and validates fields)
- Red-team exercises: generate simulated compromised credentials and validate attenuation responses and forensics packaging

Open questions / TODOs
- TTL bounds: what is max attenuation window we allow before manual review? (proposal: 7 days for automated, beyond requires human approval)
- Key rotation model for AT signatures: how to surface old KIDs to SIEM when verifying older events? (need KMS design)
- Evidence retention classification by data sensitivity: PII in raw_request_context_url must be redacted in archival copies.
- Need to finalize the canonical policy serialization format (protobuf vs canonical json).

Appendix: quick example event (human readable)
- event_id: e3b0c442-98fc-4f71-b2a1-5f2b8c2d9f04
- actor_id: service-account:ingest-worker-17
- action_requested: model.delete
- attenuation_applied: true
- attenuation_details: deny=[model.delete,model.modify];allow=[model.read];until=2024-02-15T18:44:00Z;policy_hash=sha256:9a3c...
- decision_rationale: Unusual delete attempts from single host after credential change.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally operational: expect clamps and informal TODOs. Main asks: sign off on event schema, approve phased rollout cadence, and nominate SRE/SIEM owners for ingestion support.
- Ping @Marcus Li for the canonical policy hash proto prototype and @Priya for KMS integration constraints.
